title: Original public-data customer economics and adoption-stage check
scope: Public data collection and author calculations. No interviews, surveys, outreach, rented compute or workload execution. No PDF or valuation model edits.

sampling_method.population: All three Standard Acceleron Flex CPU architectures listed in Oracle current ComputeShapes docs:Intel,AMD,Ampere.
sampling_method.selection: Complete three-family comparison within one provider/service generation. A common 4 OCPU + 32 GB allocation is applied uniformly; sensitivity covers 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 GB per OCPU. No outcome-based exclusion or claim of statistical preregistration.
sampling_method.why_same_provider: Controls listed service family, currency and retail pricing policy; avoids cross-cloud geography/discount comparisons.
held_equal: Same advertised1GbpsperOCPU network scale at this allocation
sampling_method.representativeness: Oneprovider,threecurrentofferings; intentionally bounded descriptive cross-section, not a random or market-share sample.

A4_normalization_verification.current_docs: Compute Shapes, OCPUs and vCPUs section and VM.Standard.A4.Ax processor row: 1 OCPU provides 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs.
A4_normalization_verification.dated_contract_definitions: October 8, 2026 price list, printed page 120, explicitly includes A4 Ax in the 2 physical cores per OCPU exceptions.
A4_normalization_verification.older_A1: A1 remains 1 core / 1 vCPU per OCPU and is excluded from this three-family basket.

AMD.interpretation: Intel cheaper below this memory/OCPU ratio, rival cheaper above, at equal OCPU allocation. Workload performance is not equalized.

Ampere.interpretation: Intel cheaper below this memory/OCPU ratio, rival cheaper above, at equal OCPU allocation. Workload performance is not equalized.

workload_break_even.formula: Intel cost/completed task <= rival if Intel successful throughput / rival successful throughput >= Intel hourly price / rival hourly price, holding work, quality and servicelevel constant.
workload_break_even.meaning: These are break-even requirements, not measured performance advantages or deficits.

findings: CPU-line prices alone reverse the full-basket ranking. Intel has a lower CPU rental line item than AMD or Ampere, but at32GB total memory the combined bill is2.89% above AMD and19.61% above Ampere.
The 2.89% Intel/AMD premium is small enough that a modest workload-specific performance difference can reverse value ranking. This does not establish an Intel pricing disadvantage.
Memory line items account for88.46%,86.23%,77.96% of the selected Intel/AMD/Ampere bills. These are retail charge allocations, not hardware costshares.

Oracle X12 availability, planned X14, and AWS Intel regional expansion oppose an Intel-irrelevance thesis. Alternative Arm offerings and Meta agreement establish meaningful choice, not measured Intel displacement.
IBIDEN evidence supports both investment requirements and persistent scarcity rents. It cannot independently calibrate our35%matureDCAImargin orIntelannualcapex.

model_use.reason: No identified mapping from cloud retail prices/adoption announcements to Intel chip ASP, acceptedunitcapacity, volumeor margin. Keep as external check and falsification evidence.
model_use.direction: Mixed; weakens a simplistic structuralbear case more than it validates the exact forecast.

recommended_deck_exhibit.headline: Customer value depends on completed work, not CPU list prices.
recommended_deck_exhibit.takeaway: Intel needs2.9% higher successful throughput than AMD to match rental costper task. No workload was rerun; catalogue pricing doesnot identifyIntelchippricing ormargins.
recommended_deck_exhibit.footnote: Author calculation fromOracleNov2pricingAPI, cross-checkedOct8officiallist pp54-56 andcurrentshapedocs; retailprices, notchipASPs. Allforecastsunchanged.

remaining_research_gap: No original interviews and no proprietarycustomerprocurementdata. A defensible next empirical test would measurecompleted tasks andlatencyonmatcheddeployments, butwouldrequireshardware/cloudbudget andscopedauthorization; no such resources spent.
